content.title: Arithmetic Operations with Complex Numbers
content.overview: This lesson covers how to perform addition, subtraction, and multiplication with complex numbers. The focus is on treating the imaginary unit 'i' as a variable during expansion and then applying the fundamental identity i^2 = -1 to simplify the result into standard form (a + bi).
learning_objectives: Identify the real and imaginary parts of a complex number.
Perform addition and subtraction by combining like terms.
Multiply complex binomials using the FOIL method.
Apply the identity i^2 = -1 to simplify expressions.
Express final results in the standard form a + bi.

sections.title: Understanding Complex Numbers
sections.content: A complex number is written in the form a + bi, where 'a' is the real part and 'bi' is the imaginary part. The letter 'i' represents the square root of -1. When performing arithmetic, you treat 'i' much like a variable (such as x), with one critical difference: whenever you encounter i^2, you must replace it with the real number -1.

sections.title: Addition and Subtraction
sections.content: To add or subtract complex numbers, simply combine the real parts and the imaginary parts separately. For example, (a + bi) + (c + di) = (a + c) + (b + d)i. If subtracting, remember to distribute the negative sign to both the real and imaginary parts of the second complex number.

sections.title: Multiplication and the FOIL Method
sections.content:
When multiplying two complex binomials, use the FOIL method (First, Outer, Inner, Last). For (a + bi)(c + di), the steps are: 1. Multiply the First terms (ac). 2. Multiply the Outer terms (adi). 3. Multiply the Inner terms (bci). 4. Multiply the Last terms (bdi^2). After FOILing, you will have a term containing i^2. Because i^2 = -1, the term bdi^2 becomes -bd. Finally, combine the new real terms and the imaginary terms to reach the form a + bi.

![A flow chart showing the steps: FOIL binomials, Replace i^2 with -1, Group real and imaginary terms, Simplify to a+bi.](https://img.justsolvely.com/followUpImage/04e7a99f-d5ef-459c-bd5a-b20c2785ce5f-1786505453402-779.webp)

worked_examples.question: Simplify the expression: (3 + 2i)(1 - 4i) + (5 - 3i)
worked_examples.solution: Step 1: FOIL the first two binomials. (3)(1) + (3)(-4i) + (2i)(1) + (2i)(-4i) = 3 - 12i + 2i - 8i^2. Step 2: Combine the imaginary terms in the product. 3 - 10i - 8i^2. Step 3: Replace i^2 with -1. 3 - 10i - 8(-1) = 3 - 10i + 8. Step 4: Combine real terms. 11 - 10i. Step 5: Add the remaining complex number (5 - 3i). (11 + 5) + (-10i - 3i) = 16 - 13i.

common_mistakes: Forgetting to change the sign when replacing i^2 with -1 (e.g., leaving -8i^2 as -8 instead of +8).
Failing to distribute a subtraction sign to the imaginary part of a binomial.
Combining real and imaginary parts into a single term (e.g., saying 5 + 3i = 8i).
exam_tips: Always look for i^2 immediately after multiplying; it is the most common source of sign errors on the ACT.
Treat 'i' as a variable until the very last simplification step.
Standard form is always a + bi; if your answer looks different, check your real/imaginary groupings.
content.recap: To master complex number arithmetic, remember to FOIL binomials, replace every i^2 with -1, and combine real parts with real parts and imaginary parts with imaginary parts.

knowledge_claims.content: A complex number is expressed in the standard form a + bi, where 'a' is the real part and 'bi' is the imaginary part.
The imaginary unit i is defined such that i^2 is equal to -1.
To add complex numbers, add the real parts together and the imaginary coefficients together separately.
To multiply two complex binomials, use the FOIL method: First, Outer, Inner, and Last.
A common error is treating i^2 as 1 instead of -1, which leads to incorrect signs in the real part of the product.
After multiplying two complex binomials, the resulting expression should be simplified until only one real term and one imaginary term remain.
When subtracting (5 - 3i), you must subtract 5 and add 3i to the preceding terms.
The term -8i^2 simplifies to the real number +8 because -8 multiplied by -1 equals 8.
In the expression (a + bi)(c + di), the 'Last' term of FOIL (bdi^2) always contributes to the real part of the final answer.
Real numbers and imaginary numbers cannot be combined into a single term; they must remain separate as a + bi.
When simplifying (3 - 10i) + (5 - 3i), group the real terms (3 + 5) and the imaginary terms (-10i - 3i) to get 8 - 13i.
Unlike variables like 'x', the unit 'i' changes into a real number constant when raised to the second power.
